q: What is the capital of France?
fact: Paris is home to the Eiffel Tower, which was completed in 1889.

q: What is the capital of Japan?
fact: Tokyo was known as Edo until it became the imperial capital in 1868.

q: Which is the largest ocean on Earth?
fact: The Pacific Ocean covers more area than all of Earth's land combined.

q: Which mountain is the highest above sea level on Earth?
fact: Mount Everest grows a few millimeters taller each year due to tectonic movement.

q: Which is the largest hot desert in the world?
fact: The Sahara is almost as large as the entire United States.

q: What is the capital of Canada?
fact: Ottawa was chosen as Canada's capital by Queen Victoria in 1857.

q: Which river flows through Egypt to the Mediterranean Sea?
fact: The Nile is generally considered the longest river in the world.

q: What is the capital of the U.S. state of California?
fact: Sacramento became California's state capital in 1854.

q: Which of the Great Lakes is the largest by surface area?
fact: Lake Superior is the largest freshwater lake in the world by surface area.

q: The Grand Canyon is located mainly in which U.S. state?
fact: The Grand Canyon is about 277 miles long and up to 18 miles wide.

q: What is the capital of Italy?
fact: Rome is often called the Eternal City and was founded, according to legend, in 753 BCE.

q: Which was the first national park established in the United States?
fact: Yellowstone, established in 1872, is famous for its geysers and hot springs.

q: The Mississippi River flows into which body of water?
fact: The Mississippi River drains water from all or parts of 31 U.S. states.

q: What is the capital of the U.S. state of Texas?
fact: Austin is home to the largest urban bat colony in North America, under the Congress Avenue Bridge.

q: What is the capital of Australia?
fact: Canberra was purpose-built as Australia's capital and became the seat of government in 1927.

q: Which river is generally considered the longest in the United States?
fact: The Missouri River flows about 2,341 miles before joining the Mississippi River.

q: What is the capital of South Korea?
fact: Seoul has been a capital city for more than 600 years.

q: Mount Kilimanjaro, the highest mountain in Africa, is located in which country?
fact: Kilimanjaro is a dormant volcano and the tallest free-standing mountain in the world.

q: Which country contains the largest share of the Amazon rainforest?
fact: About 60 percent of the Amazon rainforest lies within Brazil.

q: What is the capital of the U.S. state of New York?
fact: Albany is one of the oldest continuously chartered cities in the United States, chartered in 1686.

q: Which mountain range runs along the eastern side of the United States?
fact: The Appalachian Mountains are among the oldest mountain ranges on Earth.

q: What is the capital of Norway?
fact: Oslo was founded around 1048 and was once called Christiania.

q: Death Valley, one of the hottest places on Earth, is located mainly in which U.S. state?
fact: Death Valley holds the record for the highest air temperature reliably recorded on Earth, 134 degrees Fahrenheit in 1913.

q: Which river forms a large part of the border between the United States and Mexico?
fact: The Rio Grande is known as the Rio Bravo in Mexico.

q: What is the capital of Argentina?
fact: Buenos Aires is famous for its wide avenue, 9 de Julio, one of the widest in the world.

q: What is the capital of Iceland?
fact: Reykjavik is the world's northernmost capital of a sovereign state.

q: Lake Baikal, the deepest freshwater lake in the world, is located in which country?
fact: Lake Baikal contains roughly one-fifth of the world's fresh surface water.

q: Denali, the highest peak in North America, is located in which U.S. state?
fact: Denali rises to 20,310 feet above sea level.

q: What is the capital of Kazakhstan?
fact: Astana was renamed Nur-Sultan in 2019 and changed back to Astana in 2022.

q: Which European capital city lies on the Danube River?
fact: The Danube flows through four European capitals: Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest, and Belgrade.

q: The Atacama Desert, one of the driest places on Earth, lies mainly in which country?
fact: Some parts of the Atacama Desert receive almost no recorded rainfall for years at a time.

q: Mount Aconcagua, the highest mountain outside Asia, is located on which continent?
fact: Aconcagua, in Argentina, rises to about 22,841 feet above sea level.

q: What is the capital of Mongolia?
fact: Ulaanbaatar is often considered the coldest capital city in the world by average annual temperature.

q: The Sargasso Sea, known for having no land coastline, is part of which ocean?
fact: The Sargasso Sea is defined by ocean currents rather than by land boundaries.

q: The Strait of Gibraltar separates Spain from which African country?
fact: At its narrowest point, the Strait of Gibraltar is only about 8 miles wide.
